```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(hypermodR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
```
The workbench uses the same R objects and numerical functions. Its synthetic
example predicts continuous response with subject-grouped folds. Opening the
app does not install runtimes or download weights.

```{r app-state}
state <- hm_app_state()
if (!isTRUE(all(identical(state$status, "empty")))) {
  cli::cli_abort("Example assertion failed.", class = "hm_example_error")
}
x <- hm_example()
if (!isTRUE(all(methods::validObject(x)))) {
  cli::cli_abort("Example assertion failed.", class = "hm_example_error")
}
```

```{r launch, eval=FALSE}
hm_app(launch = TRUE, host = "127.0.0.1", port = NULL)
```

Use `hm_app(launch = FALSE)` to construct a `shiny.appobj` without starting a
server. Import an RDS `HMDataset`/`HMSequence` or start with the synthetic example, inspect wavelength and grouping metadata,
choose the supported task/model and training recipe, run, inspect the held-out
metrics, and export the reproducible configuration/results. A changed input or
configuration invalidates stale results. Keep subject IDs in split metadata;
individual spectra are not independent biological units.

`hm_submit_job()` starts an owned background job; `hm_job_status()` inspects it
and `hm_cancel_job()` cancels that owned job. `hm_export_result()` writes a new
export directory. Default exports omit individual-level data; private exports
require an explicit request. Read persisted package runs with `hm_read_run()`
and reproduce their task/workflow/split in an R script.

UI/server tests and real browser workflows are separate evidence. Full keyboard,
focus, both colour modes, narrow layout, cancellation/recovery, two-session
isolation and app-to-script equality must be inspected in a real browser before
claiming browser qualification. Optional app dependencies are Shiny, bslib,
callr and processx. The shared website uses themakR; the app uses bslib directly.

The current workbench supports grouped regression/classification with R engines.
Prepare ROI reductions through the API before import; an interactive annotation
editor is outside this workbench. Runtime metadata resolution, terms review and
installation are explicit user actions.
